bull.b: Teradyne's high gross margins (near 58%) and healthy operating margins reflect durable pricing power and mix advantages from high-value semiconductor test systems. Sustained margins support reinvestment, R&D and returns through the next several quarters even if volumes fluctuate.

A large and growing AI-driven mix expands Teradyne's TAM for test equipment; coupled with new platforms (Photon 100, Omnyx) and merchant GPU production wins, this structural demand should drive multi-quarter revenue momentum and deeper design-ins across customers.

bull.t: Conservative Balance Sheet and High Returns
bull.b: Modest leverage and ~20% ROE provide financial flexibility to fund incremental capex, product ramps and selective M&A without overextending the balance sheet, helping manage semiconductor cyclicality and support strategic investments over the medium term.

bear.b: High reliance on a few very large, vertically-integrated customers increases revenue volatility and bargaining risk. Large, lumpy orders can produce sharp swings in quarterly results and working capital needs, complicating capacity planning and multi-quarter revenue visibility.

Management's disclosure that a majority of revenue is first-half weighted highlights execution and timing risk for the back half. This structural seasonality and constrained visibility make forecasting, inventory and capacity allocation more challenging across the next 2–6 months.

Free cash flow has converted at ~two-thirds of net income recently, but inconsistency and unusually large TTM cash figures raise confidence concerns. Variable cash conversion limits durable funding for capex, dividends and M&A without leaning on external financing in weaker quarters.
